newsitem.title: USA: US T-bond extends gains, yld lowest since April 4.
newsitem.headline: US T-bond extends gains, yld lowest since April 4.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries extended gains in late trading as a new batch of economic data suggested inflation remained mostly subdued, analysts said.

The 6-3/4 percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond jumped two full points to 100-28/32. Its yield dropped to 6.68 percent, the lowest level since 6.66 percent registered at the close of business on April 4.
Prices rallied across the yield curve as traders detected a broad-based spectrum of buyers, ranging from retailers to speculators to some longer-term investors.

The rally was mostly trigerred by the release of a lower-than-expected rise in the Employment Cost Index (ECI) for the third quarter. The gauge rose 0.6 percent against an expected 0.8 percent increase.
Analysts said the subdued figure suggested inflation is likely to remain mostly in check in the near future.
"The market has been very, very bullish today," said a trader at a primary dealership. "I'm impressed. The rally has been very strong," he added.
